entities.summary: Carolyn Beatrice Parker was a research physicist and educator whose scientific contributions helped expand our understandings of physics and aircraft radio technologies during WWII. After obtaining her undergraduate degree at Fisk University, in 1938, Parker taught at public schools in Florida before attending the University of Michigan to earn a M.A. in physics in 1941. From 1943 to 1947, Parker contributed to the war effort by working in the Aircraft Radio Laboratory and subsequently returned to Fisk University as an assistant professor.
